A module connector is provided for connecting a first solar module to a second solar module. The connector includes a first connector part configured to engage and secure the first solar module, and a second connector part configured to engage and secure the second solar module.

The first connector part secures the first solar module by holding a portion of the module frame between a tilted top flange and a hook-shaped bottom component. The tilted top flange bears against an upper region of the frame, while the hook-shaped bottom component engages a lower region of the frame. In particular, the hook-shaped bottom component is shaped to slide around and enclose an inner side of the bottom portion of the first solar module’s frame, thereby retaining the first solar module in position.

The second connector part is arranged in a similar manner for securing the second solar module. The second connector part includes a tilted top flange, a hook-shaped bottom component, and a fastener. The tilted top flange and the hook-shaped bottom component cooperate to clamp or retain a portion of the second solar module’s frame, while the fastener helps secure the second connector part in its engaged position.

The connector further includes a third fastener that joins the top component of the first connector part to the bottom component of the second connector part. By fastening these components together, the connector mechanically links the first and second solar modules and maintains them in a desired relative position.
outputs.L4:
A module connector is provided for mechanically joining a first solar module to a second solar module positioned adjacent to it. The connector includes two cooperating connector parts, each formed with an upper component and a lower component. The upper components are arranged to engage the upper regions of the module frames, while the lower components are shaped to engage the lower regions of the module frames. In particular, each upper component includes a tilted top flange configured to bear against or overlie a corresponding portion of a solar module frame. Each lower component includes a hook-shaped lower end that can be slid around or beneath the bottom edge of the module frame so that the connector part captures the frame from below.

During installation, a first connector part is positioned on the frame of the first solar module, and a second connector part is positioned on the frame of the second solar module. The hook-shaped bottom ends are slid into place around the bottom portions of the respective module frames, while the tilted top flanges are aligned with the upper frame portions. Fasteners are then tightened to clamp the upper and lower components against the module frames, thereby securing each connector part to its respective module. The fasteners may extend through aligned openings in the connector components and may be tightened to apply a clamping force that holds the modules firmly without requiring modification of the module frames.

After the first and second connector parts have been attached to the corresponding solar modules, the connector parts are fastened to one another. This fastening operation draws the adjacent modules into a secure relative position and creates a stable mechanical link between them. By engaging both the top and bottom regions of each module frame, the connector resists separation, shifting, and relative movement between the modules. The paired top-and-bottom construction, the tilted top flanges, the hook-shaped lower ends, and the clamping fasteners together provide a reliable connection suitable for joining neighboring solar panels in an array.
outputs.L5:
A module connector is an interface or component used to link separate modules within a larger system. Its main purpose is to allow different parts of a device, machine, or software platform to communicate and work together efficiently. By using a module connector, developers and engineers can build systems that are easier to assemble, maintain, upgrade, and repair.

In hardware, a module connector may refer to a physical connection point, such as a plug, socket, pin header, or terminal block. These connectors are commonly used in electronics, industrial equipment, computers, and automation systems. They help transfer power, data, or signals between modules without requiring permanent wiring. This makes replacement or expansion much simpler.

In software, a module connector can describe the logical connection between different software modules. It may define how data is exchanged, how functions are called, or how services interact. For example, APIs, middleware, and communication protocols can all act as module connectors in a software architecture.

A good module connector should be reliable, compatible, and easy to use. It should provide a stable connection while supporting flexibility and scalability. Whether used in electronic devices or software systems, a module connector plays an important role in creating modular, efficient, and adaptable designs.

Each connector part has a hook-shaped lower end. The hook-shaped lower ends are designed to slide around or engage beneath the bottom portions of the respective solar module frames, so that the connector parts can be positioned securely on the frame edges without requiring access through the module body.

After the first and second connector parts are placed on the adjacent module frames, the parts are joined together using multiple fasteners. The fasteners clamp or lock the connector parts relative to one another, thereby holding the two solar modules in an aligned, mechanically connected relationship. This arrangement helps provide a stable connection between neighboring solar panels while allowing installation by sliding the hooked portions around the lower frame edges and then tightening the fasteners.

Each connector part has an upper component positioned near the top side of the solar panel modules. The upper components include flanges that extend outward and are tilted slightly downward. These downward-tilted flanges help press against and retain the solar panel module frames, improving grip and stability.

Each connector part also has a lower component positioned beneath the upper component. The lower components include hook-shaped ends configured to engage with a support structure, rail, frame, or corresponding portion of the connector. The hook-shaped ends help resist lifting or separation of the solar panel modules after installation.

Fasteners extend through or between the connector parts to secure the solar panel modules and to connect the first and second connector parts together. When the fasteners are tightened, the upper flanges clamp the solar panel modules while the lower hook-shaped ends provide additional mechanical engagement. This arrangement allows the connector to hold neighboring solar panel modules securely, resist movement caused by wind or vibration, and simplify installation of a solar panel array.
